paragraphs.sourceText: It’s quite remarkable how different genres of music can spark unique feelings, emotions, and memories. Studies have shown that music can reduce stress and anxiety before surgeries and we are all attracted toward our own unique life soundtrack.

paragraphs.sourceText: If you’re looking to 26 stress, you might want to give classical music a try.

paragraphs.sourceText: The sounds of classical music produce a calming effect letting 27 pleasure-inducing dopamine (多巴胺) in the brain that helps control attention, learning and emotional responses. It can also turn down the body’s stress response, resulting in an overall happier mood. It turns out a pleasant mood can lead to 28 in a person’s thinking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 古典音乐的声音产生镇定效果，释放大脑中令人愉悦的多巴胺（多巴胺），有助于控制注意力、学习和情绪反应。它还可以降低身体的压力反应，从而带来整体快乐的心情。事实证明，愉快的心情可以使人的思维清晰。

paragraphs.sourceText: Although there are many great 29 of classical music like Bach, Beethoven and Handel, none of these artists’ music seems to have the same health effects as Mozart’s does. According to researchers, listening to Mozart can increase brain wave activity and improve 30 function. Another study found that the distinctive features of Mozart’s music trigger parts of the brain that are responsible for high-level mental functions. Even maternity 31 use Mozart to help newborn babies adapt to life outside of the mother’s belly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管有许多伟大的古典音乐作曲家，如巴赫、贝多芬和亨德尔，但这些艺术家的音乐似乎都没有莫扎特的音乐具有同样的健康功效。研究人员称，听莫扎特可以增加脑电波活动并改善认知功能。另一项研究发现，莫扎特音乐的独特特征触发了大脑中负责高级心理功能的部分。甚至产科病房也使用莫扎特来帮助新生婴儿适应母亲肚子外的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: It has been found that listening to classical music 32 reduces a person’s blood pressure. Researchers believe that the calming sounds of classical music may help your heart 33 from stress. Classical music can also be a great tool to help people who have trouble sleeping. One study found that students who had trouble sleeping slept better while they were listening to classical music.

paragraphs.sourceText: Whether classical music is something that you listen to on a regular basis or not, it wouldn’t 34 to take time out of your day to listen to music that you find 35 . You will be surprised at how good it makes you feel and the potentially positive change in your health.

paragraphs.sourceText: The Curious Case of the Tree That Owns Itself
paragraphs.translationZh: 拥有自己的树的奇事

paragraphs.sourceText: A) In the city of Athens, Georgia, there exists a rather curious local landmark — a large white oak that is almost universally stated to own itself. Because of this, it is considered one of the most famous trees in the world. So how did this tree come to own itself and the land around it?
paragraphs.translationZh: A）在佐治亚州雅典市，有一个相当奇怪的当地地标——一棵几乎普遍声称拥有自己的大白橡树。因此，它被认为是世界上最著名的树木之一。那么这棵树是如何拥有自己和它周围的土地的呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Sometime in the 19th century a Georgian called Colonel William Jackson reportedly took a liking to the said tree and endeavored to protect it from any danger. As to why he loved it so, the earliest documented account of this story is an anonymously written front page article in the Athens Weekly Banner published on August 12, 1890. It states, “Col. Jackson had watched the tree grow from his childhood, and grew to love it almost as he would a human. Its luxuriant leaves and sturdy limbs had often protected him from the heavy rains, and out of its highest branches he had many a time gotten the eggs of the feathered singers. He watched its growth, and when reaching a ripe old age he saw the tree standing in its magnificent proportions, he was pained to think that after his death it would fall into the hands of those who might destroy it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 据报道，在 19 世纪的某个时候，一位名叫威廉·杰克逊上校的格鲁吉亚人很喜欢这棵树，并努力保护它免受任何危险。至于他为何如此喜爱这棵树，最早有记载的记载是 1890 年 8 月 12 日出版的《雅典周刊》头版的一篇匿名文章。文章中写道：“杰克逊上校从小就看着这棵树长大，他几乎像爱人类一样爱着它。它茂盛的叶子和粗壮的四肢经常保护他免受大雨的侵袭，他多次从最高的树枝上得到羽毛歌手的蛋。他看着这棵树。”当他年老时，他看到这棵树以其宏伟的比例矗立着，他痛苦地想到在他死后它会落入那些可能摧毁它的人的手中。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Towards this end, Jackson transferred by means of a deed ownership of the tree and a little land around it to the tree itself. The deed read, “W. H. Jackson for and in consideration of the great affection which he bears the said tree, and his great desire to see it protected has conveyed unto the said oak tree entire possession of itself and of all land within eight feet of it on all sides.”
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 为此，杰克逊通过契约将这棵树及其周围的一小块土地的所有权转让给了这棵树本身。契约上写着：“W.H.杰克逊出于对这棵树的深切感情，以及他希望看到这棵树得到保护的强烈愿望，已将其全部所有权转移给了这棵橡树，以及它周围八英尺范围内的所有土地。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D) In time, the tree came to be something of a tourist attraction, known as The Tree That Owns Itself. However, in the early 20th century, the tree started showing signs of its slow death, with little that could be done about it. Father time comes for us all eventually, even our often long lived, tall and leafy fellow custodians (看管者) of Earth. Finally, on October 9, 1942, the over 30 meter tall and 200 - 400 year old tree fell, rumor has it, as a result of a severe windstorm and/or via having previously died and its roots rotted.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 随着时间的推移，这棵树成为了一个旅游景点，被称为“拥有自己的树”。然而，在 20 世纪初，这棵树开始出现缓慢死亡的迹象，但对此却无能为力。我们所有人的父亲时代最终都会到来，甚至包括我们那些长寿、高大、绿叶的地球守护者（看管者）。最终，1942 年 10 月 9 日，这棵 30 多米高、200 至 400 年树龄的树倒塌了，有传言称，这是由于一场严重的风暴和/或之前已经死亡且根腐烂了。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) About four years later, members of the Junior Ladies Garden Club (who’d tended to the tree before its unfortunate death) tracked down a small tree grown from a nut taken from the original tree. And so it was that on October 9, 1946, under the direction of Professor Roy Bowden of the College of Agriculture at the University of Georgia, this little tree was transplanted to the location of its ancestor. A couple of months later, an official ceremony was held featuring none other than the Mayor of Athens, Robert L McWhorter, to commemorate the occasion.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 大约四年后，少年女士花园俱乐部的成员（在这棵树不幸去世之前一直在照料这棵树）找到了一棵小树，它是用从原来的树上取下的坚果长成的。就这样，1946年10月9日，在佐治亚大学农学院罗伊·鲍登教授的指导下，这棵小树被移植到了它祖先的位置。几个月后，雅典市长罗伯特·L·麦克沃特 (Robert L McWhorter) 出席了一场正式仪式来纪念这一时刻。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) This new tree became known as The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself and it was assumed that, as the original tree’s heir, it naturally inherited the land it stood on. Of course, there are many dozens of other trees known to exist descending from the original, as people taking a nut from it to grow elsewhere was a certainty. That said, to date, none of the original tree’s other children have petitioned the courts for their share of the land, so it seems all good. In any event, The Son of the Tree That Owns Itself still stands today, though often referred to simply as The Tree That Owns Itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 这棵新树被称为“拥有自己的树的儿子”，人们认为，作为原树的继承人，它自然继承了它所站立的土地。当然，还有许多其他已知的树是从原始树衍生而来的，因为人们肯定会从中取出坚果种植在其他地方。也就是说，到目前为止，原树的其他孩子都没有向法院请求获得他们的土地份额，所以看起来一切都很好。无论如何，“拥有自己的树之子”至今仍然屹立不倒，尽管经常被简单地称为“拥有自己的树”。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) This all brings us around to whether Jackson ever actually gave legal ownership of the tree to itself in the first place and whether such a deed is legally binding.
paragraphs.translationZh: G）这一切都让我们思考杰克逊是否实际上首先将这棵树的合法所有权赋予了自己，以及这样的契约是否具有法律约束力。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Well, to begin with, it turns out Jackson only spent about three years of his life in Athens, starting at the age of 43 from 1829 to 1832, sort of dismissing the idea that he loved the tree from spending time under it as a child and watching it grow, and then worrying about what would happen to it after he died. Further, an extensive search of land ownership records in Athens does not seem to indicate Jackson ever owned the land the tree sits on.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 嗯，首先，杰克逊从 43 岁开始，从 1829 年到 1832 年，只在雅典度过了大约三年的时间，他在某种程度上否认了他热爱这棵树的想法，因为他小时候在这棵树下度过了时光，看着它长大，然后担心他死后它会发生什么。此外，对雅典土地所有权记录的广泛搜索似乎并没有表明杰克逊曾经拥有这棵树所在的土地。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) He did live on a lot of land directly next to it for those three years, but whether he owned that land or not isn’t clear. Whatever the case, in 1832 a four acre parcel, which included the land the tree was on and the neighboring land Jackson lived on, among others, was sold to University professor Malthus A Ward. In the transaction, Ward was required to pay Jackson a sum of $1,200 (about $31,000 today), either for the property itself or simply in compensation for improvements Jackson had made on the lot. In the end, whether he ever owned the neighboring lot or was simply allowed to use it while he allegedly worked at the University, he definitely never owned the lot the tree grew on, which is the most important bit for the topic at hand.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 那三年来，他确实住在紧挨着它的很多土地上，但他是否拥有那块土地还不清楚。不管怎样，1832 年，一块四英亩的土地（其中包括这棵树所在的土地和杰克逊居住的邻近土地等）被卖给了大学教授马尔萨斯·沃德 (Malthus A Ward)。在交易中，沃德被要求向杰克逊支付 1,200 美元（相当于今天的 31,000 美元），要么是为了房产本身，要么只是为了补偿杰克逊对该地段所做的改进。最后，无论他曾经拥有邻近的土地，还是只是在他据称在大学工作期间被允许使用它，他绝对从未拥有这棵树生长的土地，这是当前话题中最重要的一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) After Professor Ward purchased the land, Jackson and his family purchased a 655 acre parcel a few miles away and moved there. Ten years later, in 1844, Jackson seemed to have come into financial difficulties and had his little plantation seized by the Clarke County Sheriff’s office and auctioned off to settle the mortgage. Thus, had he owned some land in Athens itself, including the land the tree sat on, presumably he would have sold it to raise funds or otherwise had it taken as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 沃德教授购买了这块土地后，杰克逊和他的家人在几英里外购买了一块 655 英亩的土地并搬到了那里。十年后，即 1844 年，杰克逊似乎陷入了财务困难，他的小种植园被克拉克县治安官办公室没收并拍卖以偿还抵押贷款。因此，如果他在雅典拥有一些土地，包括这棵树所在的土地，他可能会出售它以筹集资金，或者以其他方式将其夺走。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) And whatever the case there, Jackson would have known property taxes needed to be paid on the deeded land for the tree to be truly secure in its future. Yet no account or record indicates any trust or the like was set up to facilitate this.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）无论情况如何，杰克逊都会知道需要在契约土地上缴纳财产税，才能使这棵树在未来真正安全。然而，没有任何账户或记录表明任何信托或类似机构是为了促进这一点而设立的。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) On top of all this, there is no hard evidence such a deed ever existed, despite the fact that deed records in Athens go back many decades before Jackson’s death in 1876 and that it was supposed to have existed in 1890 in the archives according to the original anonymous news reporter who claims to have seen it.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 最重要的是，没有确凿的证据证明这样的契约曾经存在过，尽管事实上雅典的契约记录可以追溯到 1876 年杰克逊去世之前的几十年，而且据声称见过它的最初的匿名新闻记者称，它应该在 1890 年就存在于档案中。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) As you might imagine from all of this, few give credit to this side of the story. So how did all of this come about then?
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 正如你可能从这一切中想象到的那样，很少有人相信故事的这一面。那么这一切是怎么发生的呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: N) It is speculated to have been invented by the imagination of the said anonymous author at the Athens Weekly Banner in the aforementioned 1890 front page article titled “Deeded to Itself”, which by the way contained several elements that are much more easily proved to be false. As to why the author would do this, it’s speculated perhaps it was a 19th century version of a click-bait thought exercise on whether it would be legal for someone to deed such a non-conscious living thing to itself or not.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 据推测，它是由雅典周刊横幅上上述 1890 年头版文章中的匿名作者的想象力发明的，标题为“契约本身”，顺便说一下，其中包含的几个元素更容易被证明是错误的。至于作者为什么要这么做，据推测，这可能是 19 世纪版本的点击诱饵思维练习，即某人对自己做这样一个无意识的生物是否合法。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Whatever the case, the next known instance of the Tree That Owns Itself being mentioned wasn’t until 1901 in the Centennial Edition of that same paper, the Athens Weekly Banner. This featured another account very clearly just copying the original article published about a decade before, only slightly reworded. The next account was in 1906, again in the Athens Weekly Banner, again very clearly copying the original account, only slightly reworded, the 19th century equivalent of re-posts when the audience has forgotten about the original.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 不管怎样，下一个已知的拥有自己的树的例子直到 1901 年才出现在同一篇报纸《雅典周刊横幅》的百年纪念版中。这篇文章非常清楚地介绍了另一个帐户，只是复制了大约十年前发表的原始文章，只是稍微改写了措辞。下一个报道发生在 1906 年，再次出现在《雅典周刊横幅》中，再次非常清楚地复制了原始报道，只是稍微改写了措辞，相当于 19 世纪当观众已经忘记了原始报道时的重新发布。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Jackson was said to have transferred his ownership of the oak tree to itself in order to protect it from being destroyed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 据说杰克逊将这棵橡树的所有权转让给了自己，以保护它免遭破坏。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. No proof has been found from an extensive search that Jackson had ever owned the land where the oak tree grew.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 通过广泛的搜索，没有发现任何证据表明杰克逊曾经拥有橡树生长的土地。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. When it was raining heavily, Jackson often took shelter under a big tree that is said to own itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 当下大雨的时候，杰克逊经常躲在一棵据说是自己的大树下。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. There is no evidence that Jackson had made arrangements to pay property taxes for the land on which the oak tree sat.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don’t more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?
paragraphs.translationZh: 无可辩驳的是，员工知道是非之分。那么，当更多的员工看到有人在工作场所表现出危险行为时，为什么不进行干预呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company’s culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有很多因素会影响人们是否干预。首先，他们需要能够看到危险局势开始显现。其次，公司文化需要让他们感到可以安全地畅所欲言。第三，他们需要具备有效表达能力的沟通技巧。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is not strictly a workplace problem; it’s a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect — the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it — meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
paragraphs.translationZh: 严格来说，这并不是一个工作场所问题；而是一个问题。这在工作之外也是一个日益严重的问题。每天，人们都会在街上目睹事情的发生，然后选择袖手旁观。这被称为旁观者效应——目击事件的人越多，该群体中帮助受害者的可能性就越小。这背后的心理学称为责任分散。基本上，人群越多，就越多的人认为会有其他人来处理这件事——这意味着没有人在需要的时候有效干预或采取行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don’t make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种从众心态足以让人们逃避自己已知的责任。但不仅仅是一线工人没有在工作场所进行安全干预。也有主管人员不干预的情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当一群员工发现领导层没有解决不安全行为时，就会开创先例，表明这些情况应该如何解决，从而为每个人定义安全文化。

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they’ll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don’t intervene — they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管鼓励工人在观察到不安全操作时进行干预，但这种情况发生的情况还不到一半。恐惧是不干预的最终因素。人们担心受到惩罚，担心如果他们干预，他们将不得不做更多的工作。过去不成功的尝试是人们不干预的另一个重要因素——他们倾向于在未来的所有情况下将这一行动推迟到其他人身上。

paragraphs.sourceText: On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there’s a danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在许多工作场所，必须任命有能力的工人。他们的部分工作是在工人在没有适当设备的情况下执行任务或条件不安全时进行干预。当出现危险时，合格的工人还必须停止继续工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn’t required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 主管也发挥着关键作用。即使不需要有能力的人员，主管也需要广泛的技能，不仅可以识别和减轻工作场所的危险，还可以在团队内部建立一个安全氛围，支持他们之间的干预和开放沟通。

paragraphs.sourceText: Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it’s important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you’re a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了有能力的工人和主管之外，重要的是要教育组织内的每个人，如果他们目睹了可能的不安全行为，无论您是指定的有能力的人员、主管还是一线工人，他们都有义务进行干预。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The term “environmentalist” can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: “环保主义者”一词可以有不同的含义。它曾经指的是努力保护野生动物和自然生态系统的人们。在 21 世纪，这个术语已经演变为反映应对人为气候变化的需要。

paragraphs.sourceText: The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这两种环保主义之间的区别是科学界内部关于核能的分歧的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn’t worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers’ basic demands when the sun isn’t shining and the wind isn’t blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一方面是纯粹主义者，他们认为核电不值得冒险，而解决气候危机的唯一解决方案是可再生能源。反对方同意可再生能源至关重要，但表示社会需要足够的电力来满足消费者在没有阳光和风的情况下的基本需求。核能比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多，是一种自然的选择，特别是在水力发电能力有限的情况下。

paragraphs.sourceText: Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn’t an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it’s a valuable option to have if we’re serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 帮助撰写联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会报告的莱昂·克拉克并不是核能的不加批判的支持者，但他表示，如果我们认真实现碳中和，那么核能是一个有价值的选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables,” he said. “If you don’t believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “所有这一切的核心是你认为我们能够在多大程度上利用 100% 可再生能源真正实现气候目标，”他说。 “如果你不相信我们能做到这一点，而你又关心气候，那么你就被迫考虑核能之类的东西。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been “100% renewable” for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 普遍 100% 可再生性的实现同样存在争议。佛蒙特州伯灵顿等城市多年来一直“100%可再生能源”。但这些城市往往人口较少，有时仍然依赖化石燃料能源，并且拥有大量可立即使用的可再生资源。与此同时，能够利用可再生能源的国家通常要归功于非凡的水力发电能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country’s electricity in 2019.
paragraphs.translationZh: 德国是工业化大国推动绿色能源发展的最佳案例。德国总理安格拉·默克尔 (Angela Merkel) 于 2011 年宣布了能源转型计划，这是一项能源转型计划，将逐步淘汰核电和煤炭，同时逐步采用可再生能源。自 2010 年以来，风能和太阳能发电量增长了 400% 以上，2019 年可再生能源提供了该国电力的 46%。

paragraphs.sourceText: But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn’t just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany’s north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但近年来进展已经停止。可再生能源的不稳定不仅意味着能源通常不会在夜间产生，而且太阳能和风能可能会在白天压垮电网，迫使公用事业公司向客户付费以使用其电力。落后的电网基础设施难以将过剩的绿色能源从德国北部输送到工业南部，这意味着许多工厂仍然依靠煤炭和天然气运行。一些地方也达到了政治极限，民众对新建风力涡轮机的建设提出了强烈抗议。

paragraphs.sourceText: The result is that Germany’s greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010 — slower than the EU average of 13.5%.
paragraphs.translationZh: 结果是，自 2010 年以来，德国的温室气体排放量下降了约 11.5%，低于欧盟 13.5% 的平均水平。
